- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecast tends to be too low in the first 10–15 days, then gradually increases — suggesting a lag in capturing recent price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.80 → 80.24), model overreacts and overshoots in the immediate next few days, then corrects — indicating poor handling of volatility clustering.
- Model shows weak mean reversion: fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after peaks, especially in the 15–25 day window.
- Forecast tends to be overly conservative in the final 5–10 days, underestimating the true price decline or stabilization — suggesting horizon-specific bias toward pessimism.
- Model often fails to capture the “rebound” effect after a sharp drop — underestimates recovery in the 10–15 day window.
- Forecast exhibits a persistent downward bias in the last 5–10 days of the 30-day window — may be due to model decay or insufficient weighting of recent data.
